### **1. CVE-2024-26229 (CSC.sys Client-Side Caching)**

**Vulnerable Component:** csc.sys (Client-Side Caching / Offline Files service)

**CVSS Score:** 7.8 (HIGH)  
**CWE:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow)

**Affected Versions:**
- Windows 10: versions 1507, 1607, 1809, 21H2, 22H2
- Windows 11: versions 21H2, 22H2, 23H3
- Windows Server 2008, 2012 R2, 2016, 2019, 2022

**Patch Date:** April 9, 2024 (Patch Tuesday)

**Patch Status for Win10 22H2 19045.6466:** PATCHED (patched in April 2024, well before May 2026 KB5071959)

**Exploitation Technique:**
- Improper address validation in IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER I/O Control Code
- Attackers exploit symlink (symbolic link) abuse in the CSC driver
- Write primitive: writing to arbitrary kernel addresses through improper file access permission handling
- Requires local access with low privileges; no user interaction needed

**Public PoC:**
- [michredteam/PoC-26229](https://github.com/michredteam/PoC-26229) - Windows CSC Service Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
- [RalfHacker/CVE-2024-26229-exploit](https://github.com/RalfHacker/CVE-2024-26229-exploit) - Windows LPE exploit in C

**Complexity:** Medium - Requires symlink manipulation and IOCTL knowledge

---

### **2. CVE-2023-28252 (CLFS.sys - Common Log File System)**

**Vulnerable Component:** clfs.sys (Common Log File System Driver)

**CVSS Score:** 7.8 (HIGH)  
**CWE:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) + CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write)

**Affected Versions:**
- Windows 10: versions 1507, 1607, 1809, 20H2, 21H2, 22H2
- Windows 11: versions 21H2, 22H2
- Windows Server 2022

**Patch Date:** April 11, 2023 (Patch Tuesday)

**Patch Status for Win10 22H2 19045.6466:** PATCHED (patched in April 2023, over 3 years before build 19045.6466 in May 2026)

**Exploitation Technique:**
- Out-of-bounds (OOB) read/write in `CClfsBaseFilePersisted::ExtendMetadataBlock()` and `CClfsBaseFilePersisted::WriteMetadataBlock()`
- Attackers create malformed BLF (Binary Log File) files with tampered metadata fields (`ControlRecordShadow.iExtendBlock`, `ControlRecordShadow.iFlushBlock`)
- **Type Confusion Primitive:** OOB read accesses adjacent kernel pool objects containing pointers to kernel structures
- **One-Byte Increment:** Increments value in `rgContainers[0]` array, causing it to point to a fake kernel object
- **VTable Hijacking:** Incremented pointer references user-space address (0x5000000) containing malicious virtual function table
- Windows 10 approach: Gadgets overwrite process's `PreviousMode` field to kernel mode, enabling `NtWriteVirtualMemory` calls to arbitrary kernel memory
- Windows 11 approach: Gadgets corrupt pipe object attributes, enabling arbitrary kernel access through `NtFsControlFile`
- **Final Payload:** Token theft—overwrite process's security token with SYSTEM token

**Public PoC:**
- [fortra/CVE-2023-28252](https://github.com/fortra/CVE-2023-28252) - Fortra's analysis and working PoC
- [Metasploit Module](https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/blob/master/modules/exploits/windows/local/cve_2023_28252_clfs_driver.rb) - Full Metasploit exploit module
- [duck-sec/CVE-2023-28252-Compiled-exe](https://github.com/duck-sec/CVE-2023-28252-Compiled-exe) - Compiled binary version

**Complexity:** High - Type confusion, ROP gadget usage, requires kernel object layout knowledge  
**Real-World Status:** CISA KEV catalog; actively exploited by ransomware operators

---

### **3. CVE-2024-49138 (CLFS.sys - Latest CLFS Vulnerability)**

**Vulnerable Component:** clfs.sys (Common Log File System Driver)

**CVSS Score:** 7.8 (HIGH)  
**CWE:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow)

**Affected Versions:**
- Windows 10: versions 1507, 1607, 1809, 21H2, 22H2
- Windows 11: versions 22H2, 23H2, 24H2
- Windows Server 2008 and later

**Patch Date:** December 10, 2024 (KB5048685)

**Patch Status for Win10 22H2 19045.6466:** NOT PATCHED in May 2026 build (patched in December 2024, timeline suggests it may be included in later monthly updates after May 2026)

**Exploitation Technique:**
- **Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability** via race condition in CLFS metadata processing
- Triggered by malicious BLF file with tampered metadata fields
- Vulnerabilities in `CClfsBaseFilePersisted::LoadContainerQ()` and `CClfsBaseFilePersisted::WriteMetadataBlock()`
- **Race Condition Flow:**
  1. Attacker creates malformed BLF with specific metadata to cause `ClfsEncodeBlock()` to succeed but `ClfsDecodeBlock()` to fail
  2. Failure triggers `ReleaseMetadataBlock()`, deallocating General Metadata Block from kernel memory
  3. Stale pointer remains in `CLFS_CONTAINER_CONTEXT.pContainer` field
  4. Attacker pre-allocates memory at predictable address (0x0000000002100000) with fake `CClfsContainer` object
  5. Fake object contains malicious VTable with attacker-controlled function pointers
- **VTable Hijacking:** Kernel dereferences stale pointer, loads fake object, executes fake VTable function
- **Kernel Primitives:** Arbitrary code execution in Ring 0, arbitrary read/write via `DbgkpTriageDumpRestoreState` exploitation
- **Privilege Escalation:** Modify `_EPROCESS.Token` and `_KTHREAD.PreviousMode` fields

**Public PoC:**
- [MrAle98/CVE-2024-49138-POC](https://github.com/MrAle98/CVE-2024-49138-POC) - POC exploit for CVE-2024-49138
- [Exploit-DB #52270](https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/52270) - Windows 11 23h2 CLFS.sys LPE exploit

**Complexity:** Very High - Race condition exploitation, heap manipulation, VTable hijacking  
**Real-World Status:** Detected actively exploited in the wild (CrowdStrike detection)

---

### **4. CVE-2024-21338 (appid.sys - AppLocker Driver)**

**Vulnerable Component:** appid.sys (Windows AppLocker Driver)

**CVSS Score:** N/A (approximately 6.8-7.8 based on similar vulnerabilities)  
**PR:** Low (Local Service account privileges sufficient)

**Affected Versions:**
- Windows 10
- Windows 11
- Windows Server 2019, 2022

**Patch Date:** February 13, 2024 (disclosure date; patch released in same month)

**Patch Status for Win10 22H2 19045.6466:** PATCHED (patched in February 2024, well before May 2026)

**Exploitation Technique:**
- Missing `PreviousMode` check in the IOCTL dispatcher of appid.sys
- **Vulnerability Location:** IOCTL dispatcher lacks proper validation of requests from user-mode
- **Exploit Mechanism:**
  1. Craft specially formatted IOCTL input buffer (0x18 bytes on Win10, 0x20 on Win11)
  2. Buffer contains: attacker-controlled pointer, valid file object reference, function pointer to kernel routine
  3. Exploit targets `AppHashComputeImageHashInternal()` which accepts user-controlled function pointers
  4. Use `ExpProfileDelete` (kCFG-validated kernel function) as callback target
  5. When invoked with crafted pointer, calls `ObfDereferenceObject` on current thread's PreviousMode field
  6. Decrements PreviousMode from 1 to 0
  7. Enables `NtReadVirtualMemory` and `NtWriteVirtualMemory` calls to arbitrary kernel memory
- **Kernel Read/Write Primitive:** Full kernel R/W bypassing SMEP and HVCI on Windows 10 and 11
- Can disable security products or escalate to SYSTEM
- **FudModule Rootkit Variant:** Lazarus Group used this to deploy rootkit capable of disabling AhnLab V3, CrowdStrike Falcon, HitmanPro, and Microsoft Defender

**Public PoC:**
- [Crowdfense/CVE-2024-21338](https://github.com/Crowdfense/CVE-2024-21338) - Windows AppLocker Driver (appid.sys) LPE

**Complexity:** Medium-High - Requires kernel object manipulation, function pointer exploitation  
**Real-World Status:** Actively exploited by Lazarus Group (North Korea-linked APT) as zero-day before patching

---

### **5. CVE-2025-21333 (I/O Ring Heap Buffer Overflow - Recent)**

**Vulnerable Component:** vkrnlintvsp.sys (Windows Hyper-V NT Kernel Integration VSP)

**CVSS Score:** 7.8 (HIGH)

**Affected Versions:**
- Windows 11 (Hyper-V systems)

**Patch Date:** January 2025 (Patch Tuesday)

**Patch Status for Win10 22H2 19045.6466:** N/A (Windows 10 with Hyper-V may be affected; verify with Microsoft)

**Exploitation Technique:**
- **Heap-Based Buffer Overflow** in I/O ring mechanism
- **Novel Approach:** Does NOT rely on kernel address leaks via `NtQuerySystemInformation` or `PreviousMode` manipulation
- **Heap Manipulation Technique:**
  1. Overwrite pointers in paged pool's IrRB-tagged buffer array with malicious user-space addresses
  2. Heap spraying and controlled object reallocation
  3. Target only ONE entry in array (not entire array) for reliable exploitation
  4. Array size is controllable by user, allowing heap layout control
- **Functions Exploited:** `BuildIoRingWriteFile()` and `BuildIoRingReadFile()` manipulate kernel memory
- **Kernel Primitives:** Arbitrary kernel memory read/write through I/O ring mechanism
- **Privilege Escalation:** Crafted I/O ring entry pointing to process object elevates to SYSTEM
- **Advantage:** Bypasses traditional KASLR attacks and kernel protections

**Public PoC:**
- [MrAle98/CVE-2025-21333-POC](https://github.com/MrAle98/CVE-2025-21333-POC) - POC for heap-based buffer overflow leveraging WNF state data and I/O ring

**Complexity:** Very High - Heap spraying, controlled reallocation, I/O ring API knowledge required

### **6. CVE-2025-62215 (Windows Kernel Double-Free Race Condition)**

**Vulnerable Component:** Windows Kernel (generic)

**Status:** Actively exploited as zero-day (November 2025)

**Exploitation Technique:**
- **Race Condition** leading to **Double-Free vulnerability**
- Multithreaded handle manipulation
- Heap spraying to trigger flaw under controlled conditions
- Allows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM

**Public PoC:**
- [abrewer251/CVE-2025-62215_Windows_Kernel_PE](https://github.com/abrewer251/CVE-2025-62215_Windows_Kernel_PE)
- [dexterm300/CVE-2025-62215-exploit-poc](https://github.com/dexterm300/CVE-2025-62215-exploit-poc)

**Complexity:** Very High - Race condition timing, heap corruption

### **7. CVE-2025-8061 (Lenovo Driver MSR Read/Write)**

**Exploitation Technique:**
- MSR (Model-Specific Register) read/write primitive through vulnerable Lenovo driver
- Arbitrary code execution with kernel privilege possible through LSTAR MSR overwriting
- LSTAR stores address of `KiSystemCall64()` (kernel syscall entry point)
- Redirects syscalls to attacker-controlled shellcode

**Technical Details:** [Quarkslab Blog - BYOVD to the next level](https://blog.quarkslab.com/exploiting-lenovo-driver-cve-2025-8061.html)

**Complexity:** Very High - CPU register manipulation, syscall redirection

   - I/O ring and WNF (Windows Notification Facility) data structures emerging as attack surface
   - VTable hijacking and fake object creation remain effective

   - CVE-2024-49138 (Race condition + UAF + VTable hijacking)
